rationale: outline:none and outline:none on :focus-visible suppress the UA focus ring with no visible replacement; under focus there is no focus indicator at all. F78: 'Failure of Success Criterion 2.4.7 and 1.4.11 due to removing the focus indicator or making it not visible' (here, removal).
citation: WCAG 2.2 F78 (title): 'Failure of Success Criterion 2.4.7 and 1.4.11 due to removing the focus indicator or making it not visible.'

rationale: A 3px #cccccc focus outline exists but contrasts only ~1.6:1 against the adjacent white surface, below the 3:1 non-text contrast threshold for the focus indicator.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: 'User interface components ... have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s).' G195: 'visible focus indicator ... having a 3:1 contrast ratio with adjacent colors.'

rationale: outline:none is replaced by a box-shadow ring colored #e0e0e0, which is ~1.3:1 against the adjacent white page; the replacement indicator is below 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: 'a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s).' F78 (the replacement indicator must still be visible/contrasting).

rationale: A contrasting red focus outline is authored, but the focused control's top is tucked under an opaque fixed bar (z-index:50) at rest, so the top edge of the focus ring is covered. Verified by screenshot: ring top is behind the bar while the field body remains visible. F78: focus indicator made partly 'not visible'.
citation: WCAG 2.2 F78 (title): '... due to removing the focus indicator or making it not visible.'

rationale: The focus outline is drawn outside the button (outline-offset:4px) but a tight overflow:hidden wrapper clips everything beyond the button box, removing the visible indicator. F78: indicator made not visible by clipping.
citation: WCAG 2.2 F78 (title): '... or making it not visible.'

rationale: A vivid-looking yellow (#ffeb3b) focus outline is only ~1.2:1 against the adjacent white surface; perceived saturation does not satisfy the luminance-based 3:1 requirement.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: 'a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s).'

rationale: The focus outline is offset outward into an area covered by an opaque sibling panel (z-index:5) that paints over the indicator, so it is not visible when focused. F78 occlusion.
citation: WCAG 2.2 F78 (title): '... or making it not visible.'

rationale: The focus outline color (#2962ff) equals the button color with outline-offset:0, so the indicator is 1:1 against the adjacent (button) surface and produces no visible change of appearance.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: focus indicator must have 'a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s).'

rationale: outline:none plus a #222->#444 text-color shift on focus produces no bounding focus indicator, and the color shift itself is far below 3:1, so there is no qualifying focus indicator.
citation: WCAG 2.2 F78; SC 1.4.11 Understanding 3:1 threshold for the focus indicator against adjacent colors.

rationale: outline:0 declares a high-contrast color but zero width, so nothing is painted; a color-only check could be fooled, but no indicator renders. F78: indicator effectively removed.
citation: WCAG 2.2 F78 (title): '... due to removing the focus indicator or making it not visible.'

rationale: The first chip sits flush to the left edge of an overflow:hidden strip; the left side of its outline is clipped by the container, leaving the contrasting perimeter incomplete on that edge.
citation: WCAG 2.2 F78 (title): '... or making it not visible.'

rationale: The card surface is #f5f5f5 and the focus outline is #aaaaaa, ~2.1:1 against that adjacent surface, below 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: 'a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent color(s).'

rationale: A 3px black focus outline on a white adjacent surface is 21:1, far above the 3:1 threshold and fully visible.
citation: WCAG 2.2 G195: 'Using an author-supplied, highly visible focus indicator' with '3:1 contrast ratio with adjacent colors.'

rationale: No focus CSS is authored, so the browser's default focus indicator is retained and not suppressed; relying on the UA-provided indicator is the conformant baseline.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: components 'have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1' except where 'the appearance ... is determined by the user agent and not modified by the author.'

rationale: outline:none is compensated by a #595959 box-shadow ring at ~7:1 against the adjacent white surface; the replacement indicator clears 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 G195: visible focus indicator with '3:1 contrast ratio with adjacent colors.'

rationale: A sticky header exists but the focused control is well below it; its ~5:1 #d32f2f outline is fully visible and not covered. The presence of a sticky element alone is not a failure.
citation: WCAG 2.2 F78 (failure requires the indicator to be removed or made not visible; here it remains visible).

rationale: A 3px #1a73e8 focus outline is ~4.5:1 against the adjacent white surface, above 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 G195: '3:1 contrast ratio with adjacent colors.'

rationale: The wrapper is overflow:hidden, but the indicator is an INSET white box-shadow drawn inside the button (~5.75:1 vs the #1565c0 button), so nothing is clipped and the indicator is fully visible.
citation: WCAG 2.2 G195: '3:1 contrast ratio with adjacent colors' (here ~5.75:1 against the component fill).

rationale: On a #222 page a 3px white focus outline is ~15.9:1 against the adjacent surface, far above 3:1.
citation: WCAG 2.2 G195: '3:1 contrast ratio with adjacent colors.'

rationale: Although the button is light gray (#e8e8e8), the outline is offset 3px OUTSIDE so its full perimeter sits on the white page; #0d47a1 vs white is ~8.6:1. The relevant adjacent color for an offset outline is the page, which it contrasts strongly.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: contrast measured 'against adjacent color(s)' (the offset outline is adjacent to the page).

rationale: A white-inner + #0d47a1-outer double ring guarantees a contrasting edge regardless of the adjacent color (inner ~5.75:1 vs the button, outer ~8.6:1 vs the page).
citation: WCAG 2.2 G195: robust author-supplied focus indicator with '3:1 contrast ratio with adjacent colors.'

rationale: The focus outline (#1a73e8) sits on a continuous left-to-right gradient (#f8f9fa to #0d47a1), so the adjacent color varies along the perimeter and no single deterministic ratio applies (pixel-uniform assumption fails). The runner should ABSTAIN rather than assert pass or fail. Expected human label is 'passed' because at least part of the indicator perimeter meets 3:1, but a deterministic pixel checker cannot prove it.
citation: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Understanding: contrast is 'against adjacent color(s)'; with a gradient the adjacent color is non-uniform, so automated single-ratio evaluation is not reliable.
